sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner and  learned counsel for the CBI.

2. The Petitioner is seeking pre-arrest bail in connection with CBI Vide P.S. EO-III, Delhi, arising out of F.I.R bearing R.C. No.2212023E0013 of 2023 for commission of offences punishable under Sections 120B, 420, 468, 471 read with Section 511 of IPC and under Section 6(a) of PC Act, 1988.
3. It is submitted by the learned counsel that the Petitioner is not a named accused.

The entire allegation is based on the alleged recovery of a mobile phone from the house of the co-accused,
namely, Dandi Naik.
Hence, custodial interrogation of the Petitioner is not warranted.
4. Learned retainer counsel for the CBI repelled the prayer for pre-arrest bail referring to the written objection on record.
5. It is apt to note that a copy thereof has already been served on the learned counsel for the Petitioner.

6. It is further submitted by the learned counsel that this Court had rejected the anticipatory bail application of Dandi Naik vide order dated 04.08.2025 in ABLAPL No.7301 of 2025 and there is no special feature so as to protect the Petitioner by pre-arrest bail when the investigation is in progress Subodh Tandi vs Central Bureau Of .... sentences.text: 7. The allegation against the present Petitioner is that he along with the co-accused were involved in procuring fake certificates by utilizing which the candidates applied for the post of Gramin Dak Sevak and the FIR has been instituted at the instance of Director Postal Services.

8. This Court while dealing with the anticipatory bail application of the co-accused-Dandi Naik from whose custody a mobile phone was recovered indicating chats with the present Petitioner, is not persuaded to hold that the custodial interrogation of the Petitioner is not warranted and that the Petitioner is to be protected by the expectational remedy of pre-arrest bail.
9. Taking into account the nature of allegations, this Court is not inclined to entertain the application for pre-arrest bail.

However, in the event the Petitioner surrenders before the learned Court in seisin in the aforesaid case and moves an application for his release on bail, the same shall be considered on its own merit.
Ground of parity, if any, may be considered by the learned court below.

10. It is needless to state that the observations made herein qua the allegations in respect of the Petitioner is only for the purpose of considering the pre-arrest bail applications and ought not to be construed as this Court expressing any view regarding the complicity of the Petitioners which has to be adjudicated in an independent manner.
11. Learned Court in seisin is requested to make an endeavour to dispose of the application of the Petitioner, if so, moved expeditiously.
It is needless to state following the due procedure of law.

12. The ABLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
